# Historical NVDLA firmware optimization evidence

The first full-SoC attempt used scalar byte loops for all 4096-byte poison initialization and guard comparison. It completed SDP jobs 0 through 4, then reached the actual **900.122-second wall limit**. The runner correctly retains `WALL_TIMEOUT` even though process termination returned zero. This attempt is not a passing 22-job run and is excluded from the final accepted campaigns.

A separate bounded `+verbose` run with the same ELF showed hart 0 progressing through BSS and byte-buffer initialization while hart 1 waited for ownership. It ended at its 100,001-cycle TestDriver limit. [Trace metadata and analysis](trace/analysis.json) preserve the command/result, trace hash and instruction evidence; the complete verbose trace remains an external local artifact.

The revised firmware replaces the fill and equality loops with 512 aligned 64-bit accesses while retaining every one of the 4096 bytes. A differing word is inspected byte by byte in address order using captured values, preserving the first mismatch index and exact values. `may_alias` prevents strict-aliasing violations. Scalar input generation, numerical reference calculations, valid-input checks, DMA setup and PLIC operations remain unchanged. Instruction listings show 8-byte pointer increments; this is an eightfold loop-iteration reduction, not a measured whole-program speedup claim.

The exact extracted helpers were compiled as C and C++ and checked against an independent byte-level probe: all poison bytes, equal buffers, one-byte corruption at every index with varied bit positions, and ordering when multiple bytes differ. [Probe evidence](helper-equivalence/summary.json), [source](helper-equivalence/probe.c), and [new disassembly](word-implementation.disassembly.txt) are included.

[Historical metadata](summary.json) records original/intermediate optimized source identities and original ELF hashes. `original-build/` contains the original compiler commands, logs and provenance; `original-campaign/` contains the actual bounded result and log. Complete original test-source files are preserved byte-for-byte under `original-source/`. Original Markdown is archived with a `.md.txt` suffix to preserve its bytes without implying its old relative links resolve here; the [source map](original-source-map.json) records each original name/hash. The previous standalone evidence is retained under `original-standalone/` and is superseded by the new source-bound standalone runs.

Original ELF executables and the full verbose trace remain retained in the local build directories named by metadata. They are not promised as files in this compact report. [Export hashes](export-hashes.json) distinguish original and normalized bytes. This history does not replace the final full-SoC or standalone acceptance reports.

The optimized source in this report is the historical word-helper revision, archived [byte-for-byte](optimized-source/nvdla_test.c). Both its source and simulator hashes retain their historical values. Later SDP readback checks and RTL tieoffs use a new source/model and do not change this experiment. The [original metadata](original-optimization-summary.json) is preserved; the [final-source helper probe](../helper-equivalence-final/README.md) separately verifies that these same helper definitions remain in the strengthened final firmware.
